notes.13: A minority of candidates believed that evaporation increased the speed of the remaining molecules.

notes.15: The most common error here was to confuse thermal capacity with latent heat, thus opting for distractor B .
notes.18: This question concerned thermal conduction and many candidates found it extremely difficult. The majority of candidates correctly deduced that the lowest temperature would be at end P, because of the wood’s insulating properties, but most of these believed that end R of the copper would have the highest temperature. In fact, end Q of the wood will be hottest because the heat is not conducted away from the source by the wood. This can be demonstrated by using the apparatus shown in the diagram. If a piece of / copper joint, the paper will singe on the wood side (high temperature) paper is fixed tightly around the wood but not on the copper side (lower temperature).
notes.23: A significant number of candidates believed that the plane mirror in this question would form an image at point A , apparently unaware of the position of the virtual image formed at D .
notes.24: The majority of responses to this lens question were incorrect, with distractor D (the principal focus) being particularly popular.
notes.26: This recall question on the frequency range of human hearing was quite well answered, although a significant number chose B , perhaps believing that at least one of the columns must contain an audible frequency. Candidates need to appreciate that this might not be the case, as here.
notes.30: A significant number of candidates could not identify a resistor of constant resistance from its V – I characteristic. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics June 2012
notes.31: The purpose of a relay was known by the majority of candidates, with a fair proportion of the rest opting for each of the distractors.
notes.33: The majority chose correctly in this potential divider question, with all distractors being chosen by the rest.
notes.34: This question required candidates to choose the correct fuse for a circuit, and many of the weaker candidates opted for C (10 A). The normal operating current in this circuit is 10 A, and the fuse ought to be selected with a rating slightly higher than this, hence the key D (13 A).
notes.36: Although most candidates answered this correctly, a large proportion chose B , confusing slip rings with the split rings in a commutator.
